summary: Intermittent 429s on Dedicated pool during scheduled batch warmups and health checks
description: Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent 429 (Too Many Requests) responses for a subset of requests served from their Dedicated pool. These 429s are observed primarily during the customer's scheduled batch warmup windows (hourly) and appear correlated with internal health-check probes from their orchestration tooling. Impact: NimbusDocs is seeing ~5-10% of inference requests rejected with 429s for 30-90s windows during each warmup run, causing timeouts in their downstream ingestion pipeline and degraded user experience. Environment: Dedicated GPU pool in eu-west1, reserved capacity (c4-dedicated-3), route-weighting recently changed to give background warmup traffic a separate route. Customer deployed model pins to redwood-open-7b-v1 with quantized variant for lower cost.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer schedules simultaneous warmup job with 40 parallel workers targeting /v1/generate on endpoint X at XX:00 UTC.
2) Internal orchestrator emits health-check probes (http/1.1) to the same route at the same time window.
3) Observe 429 responses from ingress for a subset of requests for 30-90s immediately after warmup start.
4) If warmup is staggered (workers start with 5s jitter) 429s frequency drops significantly.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: simultaneous fanout from warmup workers + health probes exhausts per-tenant token window on the route layer due to route-weighting not creating a fully isolated token bucket for background warmup route. SRE focused on two areas: (A) refill alignment between edge and origin token windows (we saw small drift during the minute boundary), and (B) accounting duplication when requests arrive through pooled proxy IPs (probe + warmup worker shared connection). Observed that when warmup workers were started with small jitter the 429s reduced, indicating burst alignment is the main factor. Also validated rate-limiter metrics: peak concurrent request count spiked to 420 while tenant window capacity is configured for sustained 300/sec with a 60s burst smoothing window. Related note: a recent config change to route-weighting (PR#2198) aimed to direct warmup traffic to a lower-priority route but did not enable separate quota isolation.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:05 - Support (Aisha Patel): Confirmed customer timeline and collected request IDs and sample logs. Asked for exact cron schedule and warmup worker count.

2026-03-10 10:12 - Customer (DevOps, NimbusDocs): Warmup kicks off hourly at :00 UTC. 40 workers, each does 10 short calls (1-2 tokens seed) to warm cache. We also have an internal probe job that hits /health on the same route.

2026-03-10 11:23 - SRE (Marco Chen): Reproduced a local load test against dedicated pool simulating 40x10 requests with concurrent probes. Confirmed token window exhaustion and saw refill misalignment at minute boundary on edge nodes.
2026-03-11 08:47 - Support (Aisha Patel): Implemented short-term workaround suggestion (stagger warmup start by 10s or reduce parallel workers). Customer to attempt and report.
action_items: 1) Short-term workaround: advise customer to add 5-15s jitter to warmup worker start times or reduce concurrency to 20 workers.
2) SRE task: enable route-level quota isolation for warmup route in the dedicated pool config to prevent shared token bucket exhaustion.
3) Infra task: fix refill alignment bug where edge node refill window can be off by up to 2s for certain NTP drift conditions (see INT-4302).
4) Postmortem: document recommended warmup patterns for Dedicated customers in Confluence and create a console warning when user-defined warmups exceed route burst thresholds.
resolution: Workaround applied: Customer introduced 10s jitter and halved warmup parallelism — 429s dropped to <0.5% during next runs. SRE has scheduled a config change to enable separate quota isolation for the warmup route on the customer's Dedicated pool; change targeted for 2026-03-15 with a canary rollout. Long-term fixes include a small refactor in token refill logic to reduce edge/origin drift and a console UI flag to mark routes as 'background' so they receive an isolated burst pool.
